date_note: Star's article (published 26 November, 10:57) gives no earlier day for the detentions; the date is its publication day.
exec: Star reports Turkey's intelligence agency MİT and Istanbul Police detained two suspects accused of trying to infiltrate wireless networks of critical institutions, including defense industry firms.
geo_basis: country as stated by the source
plain: Star reports that Turkish intelligence says two people mapped Wi-Fi networks in Ankara and Istanbul for a foreign intelligence service; both were jailed pending trial.
summary: Star reports that MİT and Istanbul Police detained two suspects accused of trying to infiltrate the wireless networks of critical institutions, including defense industry firms, in Ankara and Istanbul. According to the article, MİT found they acted for an unnamed foreign intelligence service. The suspects said their instructions came through social media job listings and that they were paid in cryptocurrency; both were sent to prison pending trial.
title: Star: MİT detains two suspects accused of mapping Wi-Fi networks of critical institutions for a foreign intelligence service

validation.note: Only Star was read (page text partly garbled by encoding); MİT's own statement was not read.

review.note: stronger than the source: 'recruited via job ads' now suspects' own account; exec said 'disrupted a network', now detained two suspects accused
